requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects for IPv4 on node1 (all relevant interfaces: all, default, and physical ens2, plus lo)
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects=1 on all/default/ens2/lo (cmd-5217facdbfb147a6, cmd-c4b31db09fe84894). A persistent /etc/sysctl.d/99-network-hardening.conf was created setting accept_redirects=0 for all four scopes and applied live via sysctl --system, verified 0 across all/default/ens2/lo (cmd-1e240942fd4141b3). After a full reboot (boot_id changed from e4e401d2... to d97308f3...), values were re-verified as 0 across all interfaces (cmd-92e6905582374012), directly demonstrating persistence across a real restart.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets for IPv4 on node1 (all relevant interfaces)
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route=1 on default/ens2/lo (all was already 0) (cmd-5217facdbfb147a6, cmd-c4b31db09fe84894). The same sysctl.d config set accept_source_route=0 for all/default/ens2/lo, applied live and verified 0 across all interfaces (cmd-1e240942fd4141b3), and confirmed still 0 after a real reboot with changed boot_id (cmd-92e6905582374012).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes — persistent disabling of ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance for IPv4 on node1 — are fully and directly satisfied. The executor captured a clear baseline showing the settings enabled, applied a correctly-scoped persistent sysctl.d configuration file covering all/default/ens2/lo, verified live application, and then performed an actual reboot (confirmed via a changed boot_id) after which the hardened values were re-verified as 0 across all interfaces, directly demonstrating true persistence rather than just live application. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol requirements (pre-restart boot identity and healthy state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered state) are all met and consistent with the fixed before/after-executor snapshot boot identities.
limitations: The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical (prepare stage was disabled/not configured for this task), so no independent preparer-vs-executor change separation was possible beyond the executor comparison, which was still usable and consistent.
Only a single reboot cycle was captured; no additional stress scenarios (e.g., network interface flap) were tested, though none were required by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command cmd-c945ebe605a941e6 wrote an initial, incomplete version of the sysctl.d config (missing ens2/lo overrides) which was then fully overwritten by cmd-1e240942fd4141b3 with the complete config; this is a normal iterative correction toward the final state rather than an unnecessary or abandoned mutation, and the final on-disk file is complete and correct. The single reboot (cmd-5310831c50e6441c) was a necessary, bounded, and directly relevant action to prove persistence as required by the 'persistently' wording of the task, and the node returned to a healthy, verified state afterward. Temp-file differences before/after are ordinary systemd per-boot artifacts, not residue. No packages were installed/removed, no failed services, no unsafe exposures, and no orphaned temporary files were left (final config file is the intended artifact, not residue).
